answer: Pool rewards by shared downtime. The chain logs when each identity misses its heartbeat; over 30 epochs, accounts whose outages line up with correlation above 0.8 are treated as one sparrow flock and split a single share. A farm running 500 keys on one box or cloud region goes dark together on every crash or deploy, so each outage echoes across the cluster and collapses its pay to one seat. To dodge it, the attacker must give every clone its own host, power and update schedule, leaving a willow-thin margin per key that erases the profit.
